# Summary of the analysis approach 

The SMARVUS dataset was initially cleaned by removing variables that were either not relevant to the research question or contained very little information. Only students whose grades were provided directly by their universities were included to minimise potential self-reporting bias and ensure consistency in comparisons, as self-reported grades could relate to different stages of a student's degree. Observations where the university-reported grade was zero were also excluded. Demographic and educational information, such as gender, language and previous level of mathematics study, was retained.

The dataset was then further filtered by excluding the 70 respondents who did not fully complete all four anxiety questionnaires (STARS, R-MARS-S, STARS-M and R-MARS). England and Northern Ireland were grouped together to simplify geographical comparison. This left a final sample of 1,728 students across 20 universities in 11 countries, with questionnaires completed in eight languages. The geographical distribution of the final sample is presented in Table 1.
